newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil rejects Union Pacific hostile bid.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil rejects Union Pacific hostile bid.

text.p: - Pennzoil Co. rejected a hostile, $6.4 billion cash and stock offer from leading U.S. independent energy company Union Pacific Resources Group Inc., Pennzoil Chairman James Pate said Tuesday.
"This bid is inadequate. ... It comes at a time when Pennzoil is in a position to realise the benefits of major long-term initiatives," Pate said during a telephone conference.

Fort Worth, Texas-based Union Pacific Resources in late June launched an $84-per-share cash-and-stock offer for the oil and gas company. At the time of the offer, analysts said the price was so attractive -- nearly $25 a share more than Pennzoil's stock price -- that the company would be hard-pressed to fend off the takeover.
However, Pennzoil's board of directors said in a statement Tuesday that the United Pacific Resources "proposal does not reflect the inherent value of Pennzoil."
The Houston-based company also said that "continued pursuit of Pennzoil's strategic plan will produce greater value for Pennzoil shareholders than UPR's proposal."
Pate said Pennzoil was not seeking a "white knight" to rescue the company from the clutches of Union Pacific Resources. "The best future for our company is as an independent company," he said.

Pennzoil explores for and produces crude oil and natural gas, and produces premium lubricants. It is the parent company of Jiffy Lube International, the world's largest franchiser of fast oil-change centres.
Pennzoil stock dropped $1.125 to close at $75.675 and Union Pacific Resources rose 12.5 cents to $25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
